description_full: Computacenter plc provides technology and services to corporate and public sector organizations in the United Kingdom, Germany, Western Europe, North America, and internationally. It offers procurement, specialist, software, logistical, technical, and circular technology sourcing services; IT strategy and advisory, integration, deployment, and support services; and managed services. The company also provides workplace solutions, including IT support, field and onsite support services, Productivity and Teamwork technology sourcing, modern endpoint, device lifecycle management, IT asset management, print solutions, and technology sourcing; cloud and applications solution, such as custom application, business automation, application platforms, data and AI platforms, and cloud services; infrastructure services, data center and edge platforms, relocation and migration, and operational resilience services; and software-defined (SD) wide area network service, proactive and reactive services, network automation, managed secure networking and implementation, SD campus networking, multi cloud connectivity, and data center networking and multi cloud network deployment. In addition, it offers security solutions, including service centers, integration centers, professional services hubs, and field and maintenance services. The company was founded in 1981 and is headquartered in Hatfield, the United Kingdom.

financial_summary: Computacenter plc is a mid-cap technology business with a $6.6B market cap on $12.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 31% against a 10% cost of capital — a 21-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 15% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $337M in free cash flow — roughly 3 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.91× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 19× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.7%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 60% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
